value.name: Miles drafts litigation strategy
value.description: Miles dictates legal language about litigating and arguing over child support and special education expenses.
evidence:
MILES
And of course we shall have to
litigate. Sentence. Paragraph.

MILES
-- Naturally the first concern for
both parties is the welfare of little
Wendell junior. Nevertheless, we
question whether the continuing
expenses for his special ed classes
are truly justified given the great
strides --

value.name: Wrigley reports Marilyn's divorce
value.description: Wrigley arrives late and tells Miles that Marylin Rexroth is divorced.
evidence:
WRIGLEY
I'm sorry I'm late. I was having
lunch with Ruth Rabinow's assistant.
Guess what? Marylin Rexroth is
divorced!

value.name: Miles celebrates Marilyn's divorce
value.description: Miles reacts with delight when he hears that Marylin Rexroth is divorced.

value.name: Wrigley says Marilyn is wealthy
value.description: Wrigley adds that Marylin Rexroth is extremely rich and could outspend Miles easily.
evidence:
WRIGLEY
...and I hear she's richer than
Croesus.

WRIGLEY
She could buy and sell you ten times
over.

value.name: Miles compares Marilyn to an athlete
value.description: Miles praises Marylin Rexroth as a top athlete at the peak of her power, implying she deserves her wealth.
evidence:
MILES
She deserves every penny. They pay
great athletes a fortune. Well,
Marylin Rexroth is an athlete at the
peak of her power.

value.name: Miles orders Marylin called
value.description: Miles presses the call button and instructs the receptionist to connect him to Marylin Rexroth Doyle.
evidence:
MILES
Get me Marylin Rexroth Doyle.

value.name: Miles claims Marylin owes him a meal
value.description: When Wrigley objects, Miles insists he should contact Marylin because she owes him a meal.
evidence:
MILES
She owes me a meal.

WRIGLEY
I'd stay away from her, Miles.

value.name: Miles dismisses Wrigley's warning
value.description: Miles brushes off Wrigley's caution and jokes that Kramer would not avoid Marylin the way Wrigley would.
evidence:
MILES
I know you would, Wrigley. But would
Kramer?

value.name: Receptionist connects Marylin
value.description: The receptionist announces that Mrs. Doyle is on the line for Miles.
